tone_statements.citation: Nishida, Fuminobu. 2019. [Namuyi phonology/grammar study, in Japanese]. Keio University.
tone_statements.quote: 本稿では、ナムイ語冕寧方言の音韻体系について述べる。…チベット・ビルマ語派という観点からすると、ナムイ語の音韻体系はやや複雑な部類に属すると言い得る。ナムイ語には多数の子音が存在するが、本論文で対象とするゾロ方言には、44 の音節頭子音と 25 の音節頭子音結合が存在する。ナムイ語にはまた、一連の有声有気音子音が見られる。本稿では以下、子音と母音の音素についての解説を試みる。声調に関しては稿を改めて論じたい。 [cited words carry a word-tone letter beneath them, e.g. mupu R, papi H, atsɨtsɨ L; phonetic forms carry Chao letters, e.g. ［bi˨˥］‘桃’, ［he˥˧］‘金’]
tone_statements.translation: This paper describes the phonological system of the Mianning dialect of Namuyi. ... From a Tibeto-Burman point of view the Namuyi sound system belongs to the rather complex type. Namuyi has many consonants; the Dzolo dialect treated in this thesis [sic] has 44 syllable-initial consonants and 25 initial clusters. Namuyi also has a series of voiced aspirated consonants. Below I attempt an account of the consonant and vowel phonemes. Tone I would like to discuss in a separate paper.

tone_statements.quote: There is a more systematic difference in tonal categories. Liu describes four categories: 55, 53, 31 and 13 for the Luoguodi variety. However, Libu Lakhi produces lexical items cognate to those Liu describes as 55, slightly lower that the top of his voice range, a tone we represent as 44. Furthermore, he produces items cognate to those in 31 and 13 as a single low level tone, which we represent as 11. Due to this merger (or non-split), we describe five tonal categories for the Xichang variety as high (55), middle-high (44), high-falling (53), low-rising (14) and low (11).
tone_statements.locator: p. 22, Part Two: Introduction, section 'The na53 mʑi53 Language'
tone_statements.summary: Five tones in the Xichang (dʐə11 qu11) variety: high 55, middle-high 44, high-falling 53, low-rising 14, low 11; Liu 1996 gives four (55, 53, 31, 13) for Luoguodi. All forms carry Chao tone numbers.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all three tagged portions of the deciding quotation are present verbatim at the stated places in copies we hold (Pavlík p.37 in the extracted text; Nishida p.39 and p.49 on the page scan we hold, scanned text matching modulo noise). (2) Deciding sources are a 2017 PhD descriptive grammar (Pavlík, western Namuzi) plus a 2013 phonology article (Nishida, eastern/Dzolo), both open and. both call the language tonal, and Nishida's weak root-initial stress tendency is already carried in the secondary-stress rule with the Gurung-template caveat. (3) The one clearly superior unheld work on Glottolog's list, Li (Lakhi) 2017 La Trobe PhD (726 pp; Glottolog lists it twice under 'Lakhi, Libu' and 'Li, Jianfu' — same thesis), was downloaded now from La Trobe OPAL and read: three contrastive tonemes H/M/L (/54 33 21/) with two sandhi tones, all nine disyllabic tone patterns attested (p.30, p.142, p.275-276)

sources.citation: Li, Jianfu (Libu Lakhi). 2017. A descriptive grammar of Namuyi Khatho spoken by Namuyi Tibetans. PhD thesis, La Trobe University. xxiv+726 pp. hdl 1959.9/564452, doi 10.26181/21859557.v1 (open, La Trobe OPAL).
sources.quote: p.30: 'There are three contrastive tonemes — high, middle and low. The high tone is notated as high falling /54/, middle as mid-level /33/ and low as low falling /21/'. p.142: 'Tone is the use of different pitch heights to contrast lexical or grammatical meaning. Tone sandhi is part of the inflectional system'. p.275-276: all nine disyllabic tone combinations attested (54+54 ... 21+21), 16 of 27 trisyllabic. Abstract p.xx: 'Three-way contrastive lexical tone—high, middle and low—plays an important role, with an additional two tones through sandhi processes.' No section or statement on lexical
sources.locator: p.30 (sec. 2, Table 2-4 Tone); ch.3 'Tone and Sandhi' p.142; sec. 3.5 'Tone structure' p.275-276; abstract p.xx; incidental 'stress' only at p.433 (emphatic adjective, last syllable stressed before /ɦa/) and p.705 (vowel after /da³³/ stressed).
sources.note: Largest description of the language (726 pp, native-speaker author, Praat-measured tone chapter); record rested on Pavlík's 206-pp thesis and Nishida's article without it. downloaded now: confirms tonal (3 tonemes + sandhi), silent on word stress.
